commit.messageHeadline: fix(state): reclaim interrupted SQLite staging copies
fix(state): reclaim snapshots with process-lifetime SQLite tokens
fix(state): align snapshot boundary checks with lifetime tokens
fix(state): reclaim SQLite backlogs outside async callers
fix(state): align cancellation fixture argv with Node types
fix(state): correct cancellation cleanup promise executor
fix(state): detach cancelled SQLite snapshot callers
fix(state): carry updater cancellation into staging allocation
fix(state): preserve cancellation through owned SQLite snapshots
fix(state): integrate snapshot cleanup with current Gateway lifecycle

Fixed both findings from [this review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150816#issuecomment-5713173820) in `7ea583c003e8fa4395964498dd4408128eef92c9`.

- Async allocation now runs reclamation through the existing SQLite child-process owner, sharing the sync algorithm and preserving shutdown/close handling. The 429 MiB backlog regression reduced the longest timer gap from 9,982.5 ms to 56.5 ms (100 ms bound).
- Validation now recognizes `parent/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-<pid>-…`, with the same inner token/legacy-age checks and outer-parent admission. The regression reclaims aged contents with a byte-count warning and preserves fresh contents.

Linux Testbox used the actual 2026.9.4 allocator/worker with a 512 MiB source: SIGTERM left 193 MiB; fresh recovery preserved it, and the same fixture aged to 25 hours was reclaimed to zero bytes. Source hash unchanged; lease stopped. Full proof details and limitations are in the PR body.

Changed-file checks and fresh final committed-branch autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1`) passed. The two new regressions fail before the fix and pass after it.

GitHub currently reports this pushed head as conflicting with `main`; no `pull_request` CI run has attached.

Addressed the cancellation finding from [this review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150816#issuecomment-5713173820) in `2c7d1d99762880350ec076583a5eb98e9c5b20c3`.

Each caller now has a cancellable join to the shared pass and retains its original abort reason. The last departing caller requests a stop; the worker finishes its in-flight directory before exiting. Other callers retain the pass, and a later allocation resumes unvisited directories. Reclamation is independent of the first caller’s worker scope. Direct snapshot/header, updater, and cached native-owner calls all forward cancellation into allocation; native backup work still settles before ownership releases.

All three new regressions fail before and pass after: cancellation improved from 10–12.9 seconds to 0.11–3.05 ms; the surviving caller completed; the unobserved pass left two untouched roots, then a later allocation recovered them. The broader run passed 203 tests with one platform skip; final cached-owner proof passed 51 state tests and the three regressions.

Windows shard 2 now selects these portable released-layout/settlement tests. Real signal-driven orphan and late-admission races remain the documented Windows gap; the PR body maps each coverage claim precisely.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed on the final files. Fresh committed-branch Codex autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1`) was scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings.

Merged via squash.
